claims.text: The famous Lapin Agile cabaret has a colourful history, originally operating around 1860 under the shady name 'Where the Thieves Meet'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Around 1880, its name was changed to 'Cabaret des Assassins' after a terrifying local legend claimed a gang of robbers murdered the owner's son there.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The current name finally stuck after the artist Andre Gill painted a humorous sign in 1875 depicting a nimble rabbit jumping out of a saucepan.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Unfortunately, that original iconic painting on canvas was stolen in 1893, so the one you see today is actually just a timber reproduction.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: To save the beloved venue from total demolition, the famous cabaret singer Aristide Bruant purchased the building.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It soon became the ultimate gathering spot for struggling young artists like Picasso and Modigliani, who would spend their nights passionately discussing the meaning of art.
claims.subject: self
